body:
This was triggered during an update to skops to support scipy=2, where testing for sparse arrays caused an error with `SpectralEmbedding`. This fixes the issue.

#### AI usage disclosure
<!--

https://scikit-learn.org/dev/developers/contributing.html#automated-contributions-policy

I used AI assistance for:
- Code generation (e.g., when writing an implementation or fixing a bug)
- Test/benchmark generation
- Documentation (including examples)
- Research and understanding

#### Any other comments?

Claude's summary:

<details>

SpectralEmbedding.fit (and SpectralClustering, which shares the same code path) builds its graph Laplacian from a k-NN sparse graph. Under sparse_interface="sparray", that graph ends up with int64 indices — not because scikit-learn does anything different, but because of a deliberate scipy design choice: sparse arrays (csr_array, unlike csr_matrix) never downcast index dtype based on content when built from raw (data, indices, indptr) arrays (scipy/scipy#16774). kneighbors_graph constructs its output that way, so the int64 propagates through 0.5 * (A + A.T) and csgraph_laplacian too.

The eigen_solver="arpack" branch in sklearn/manifold/_spectral_embedding.py then called check_array(laplacian, accept_sparse="csr", accept_large_sparse=False), rejecting those int64 indices — a restriction the "amg" and "lobpcg" branches in the same file don't impose. I confirmed scipy.sparse.linalg.eigsh, including the shift-invert mode used here (sigma=-1e-5), works fine with int64-indexed sparse arrays, so the restriction was just overly conservative, not load-bearing.

Fix

Dropped accept_large_sparse=False from that one check_array call in sklearn/manifold/_spectral_embedding.py:372 (defaults to True, matching the other two solver branches). Added a regression test comparing SpectralEmbedding output between sparse_interface="spmatrix" and "sparray", and a changelog fragment (doc/whats_new/upcoming_changes/sklearn.manifold/34959.fix.rst — PR number guessed as the next available; adjust once the real PR is opened).

Verified: the reproducer from the issue now passes, results match the spmatrix path bit-for-bit (up to sign), SpectralClustering is fixed too, and the full test_spectral_embedding.py / test_spectral.py / test_sparse.py suites pass.

Note: the issue speculated this pattern (sparray + accept_large_sparse=False) might affect other estimators (kmeans, svm, coordinate descent, SGD). I checked — those all wrap Cython/C code (libsvm, liblinear, sklearn's own _k_means_lloyd) that genuinely requires 32-bit index buffers, so their restriction is legitimate and out of scope here. Nothing left uncommitted has been staged/committed — let me know if you want it committed or turned into a PR.

</details>
title: FIX SpectralEmbedding to work with sparse array backend with large indices
